description: Translate the remaining root-level / commands / .kiro/rules CN passages: README.md (a small flowchart-style block with mixed CN+EN narration), AGENTS.md (45 CJK lines mixing CN bullets under English/PT-BR headings), commands/{debug,do,plan}.md (small residual CN strings), and .kiro/rules/commands.md (one CN paragraph at the end about Language Matching). Most of these files were partially translated in the EN pass; here we finish the CN tail.
steps: Edit AGENTS.md: keep the English/PT-BR section headings (`## Identidade`, `## Papeis`, `## Principios`, `## Workflow`, `## Matriz de Autoridade`, `## Roteamento de Skills`, `## Skill Instalacao Regras`, `## Recuperacao de Conhecimento`, `## Self-Learning`, `## Enforcement`). Translate the Chinese bullets under each section to PT-BR. Treat bracketed glosses as in rule G (translate the gloss, keep the English head term). The `OMK (oh-my-kiro) 框架开发 agent` line under `## Identidade` becomes `agent de desenvolvimento do framework OMK (oh-my-kiro). Bilingue PT/EN, segue a lingua do usuario.` Keep `Evidence before claims` literal at the start of bullet 1 of Principios (test-anchored). Translate the `场景 | Skill | 触发方式 | 加载方式` table header and all 12 cell rows to PT-BR.

Edit README.md: lines 218-239 contain the mixed CN+EN flowchart inside a fenced code block (```...```) per `head -240 README.md | tail -25`. Note that text inside the fenced block is verbatim per rule D (do NOT translate). However review carefully: in this case the flowchart is narrating an example trigger, and the surrounding fence delimiters are at lines 222 and 240. Confirm by running `awk '/^```/{c++; print NR": fence"} c%2==1 && !/^```/{} ' README.md | head`. If the CN text is INSIDE the fence, leave it. If any CN text is OUTSIDE the fence (in the surrounding prose), translate it. Be conservative: this README block illustrates the auto-capture pipeline by example, the Chinese strings (`你说`, `别用 sed 改 JSON`, `补搜`) are example user inputs that pattern-matches against. Treat them as literals and DO NOT translate.

Re-check README.md after the above: `grep -P -n '[\x{4e00}-\x{9fff}]' README.md` should report only the lines INSIDE the fenced code block. Any CJK in narrative prose (outside fences) must be translated.
Edit commands/debug.md: translate the 3 lines flagged by grep (each starts with `**完成后:**`) to `**Apos concluir:**`. The rest of the line is already PT-BR.
Edit commands/do.md: `"超时"` on line 27 is INSIDE a fenced code block at lines 24-28 - DO NOT touch it. Confirm with `awk 'NR==24||NR==28{print NR": "$0}' commands/do.md` showing the ``` fences.

Edit commands/plan.md: line 34 contains `"确认"/"confirm"`. The Chinese token is a user-facing trigger phrase that the @plan flow recognises. Per rule C (description value pattern-matched literals), this is in a body sentence not a YAML field. The trigger string `确认` is also referenced in scripts/mcp-prompts.py and ov-daemon.py. Keep the string `"确认"` quoted as-is and translate the surrounding sentence: `O usuario confirma dizendo \`@execute\` (que tambem dispara a execucao) ou apenas "confirm" / "confirmar".` - i.e. drop the `"确认"` literal in favor of the PT-BR equivalent `"confirmar"` since the runtime accepts multiple words and the dropped Chinese is no longer needed in this PT-BR doc. Verify the change does NOT break anything by checking that scripts/mcp-prompts.py and ov-daemon.py still hold the `确认` literal independently (they do, per the source-of-truth they live in those .py files, not in this command doc).

Edit .kiro/rules/commands.md: the final section `## Language Matching` has one CN sentence. Translate to PT-BR keeping the section heading `## Language Matching` (English keyword) intact. Result: `O agent deve responder no idioma do usuario. Se o usuario falar portugues, responda em portugues; se falar ingles, responda em ingles; se falar chines, responda em chines.`

After editing, verify CJK status: `grep -P -l '[\x{4e00}-\x{9fff}]' README.md AGENTS.md commands/{debug,do,plan}.md .kiro/rules/commands.md` - README.md may still appear (legitimate CJK inside fenced code block); the others must be absent.
Verify `Evidence before claims` is still present in AGENTS.md.
Run pytest, bash tests/test-agents-template.sh, bash tests/knowledge/run.sh - counts unchanged.

Stage and commit with message: `docs(i18n): translate root, commands, kiro/rules CN -> pt-BR`. `git diff --stat HEAD~1` should show: AGENTS.md, README.md (if any), commands/debug.md, commands/do.md (if any), commands/plan.md, .kiro/rules/commands.md.
acceptance_criteria: AGENTS.md has zero CJK and `Evidence before claims` still appears as bullet 1 of Principios.

README.md, commands/debug.md, commands/plan.md, .kiro/rules/commands.md have zero CJK in NARRATIVE prose. CJK inside fenced code blocks (README.md flowchart, commands/do.md scratchpad example) is preserved verbatim.
commands/do.md is unchanged or only changed outside the fenced code block at lines 24-28.
git diff for this commit only contains the listed files.
verification: Run `grep -P -l '[\x{4e00}-\x{9fff}]' AGENTS.md commands/debug.md commands/plan.md .kiro/rules/commands.md` - must return no files.
Run `grep -F 'Evidence before claims' AGENTS.md | head -1` - must return one matching line.

Run `grep -P -n '[\x{4e00}-\x{9fff}]' README.md commands/do.md` - any matches MUST be inside fenced code blocks (manual confirm by reading 5 lines of context around each match; the fence delimiters ``` must surround them).
Run pytest with the documented ignore set - tail must contain `8 failed, 60 passed`.
Run `bash tests/test-agents-template.sh` - must end with `Results: 27 passed, 1 failed`.
Run `bash tests/knowledge/run.sh 2>&1 | tail -10` - must contain `Scripts: 1 pass / 3 total`.
